title: Kobato.
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Kobato, a kind but naive girl with no memory of her past, must fill a magic bottle with the pain of hearts she has healed before four seasons pass so she can reach a place she longs to go. Guided by Ioryogi, a foul-tempered spirit trapped in the form of a toy dog, she helps at a struggling nursery school threatened by debt collectors. The story gradually reveals a backstory involving a war between worlds, an angel and God, and ends with a choice between her own wish and others' freedom.
life_message: A good life is spent easing others' suffering with sincere kindness, even at cost to oneself.

folkways.japan: Kobato's earnest effort under a gruff mentor and the debt-ridden family school reflect Japanese norms of perseverance (ganbaru) and obligation to those who raised you, described not judged.

delivery.evidence: Each episode turns on Kobato healing a wounded heart; ANN review (via Wikipedia) calls it charming, not preachy (to verify).

personified.ideology: hard-nosed money pressure, later revealed as protective cover

delivery.note: Apparent antagonists such as the debt collector are given hidden motives and reconciled rather than condemned (anime detail per Wikipedia; manga to verify).

winners_losers: Kobato's patient kindness wins: the nursery's people are healed and estranged characters reconcile, while cynicism and harshness soften; she is reborn and reunited with those she helped.
